chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali narrated from Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Alawi, from al-Amriki, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon them both), who said:

I asked him about a worm that falls from the latrine onto one's garment; is one permitted to pray in it? He said, 'There is no harm, unless you see a trace [of impurity], in which case you should wash it.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on praying in clothes if a worm from the toilet falls on them?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam Musa al-Kazim (AS) clarifies the distinction between the organism itself and its waste, establishing that the worm is not inherently impure (najis) but requires washing only if a visible trace of excrement is present. This ruling reflects the Shia juristic principle of 'absence of certainty' regarding impurity, allowing for ease in prayer attire. It highlights the practical application of *istishab* (presumption of continuity of purity) in daily ritual life.
